title: Rehearse a Truthful Account
status: New proposed Lesson 06 production script, 2026-10-30. No new animation or narration in this handoff.
learningOutcome: Privately rehearse a clear account grounded in what is known, distinguish personal contributions and evidence limits, and prepare to answer a specific follow-up without inventing details.

scenario.kind: Explicitly fictional authored training case, not a learner biography or a real admission interview

facts.text: Three volunteers prepared a one-page visitor guide for a community open afternoon.
The case participant drew the map. Maya listed session times. Noah assembled the guide.
The day before the event, the participant noticed that the map said Studio B while Maya's schedule said Blue Room.
The participant did not know whether those names meant the same room and asked the event coordinator rather than guessing.
The coordinator confirmed that both names referred to the same room and that its door sign said Blue Room.
The participant changed the map label to Blue Room and told Maya and Noah. Maya checked the schedule; Noah assembled the updated guide.
During the event, the participant saw one visitor use the map to find Blue Room.
There was no visitor survey or total count of people helped. No comparison shows what would have happened without the change.
In reflection, the participant would agree a shared list of room names earlier next time. This is a proposed future change, not an action already taken.

unknowns: Whether anyone else used the map successfully
Whether a visitor would have found the room without this change
Whether the guide made the whole event successful
How long checking with the coordinator took
Any awards, numerical impact, leadership appointment or wider achievement
scenario.permittedDecisionReason: Conflicting labels could confuse visitors; confirming the door-sign name avoided choosing a name without checking. This is the participant's stated reasoning, not a measured causal result.

roles.maya: Follow-up partner in a later authored rehearsal; also the schedule volunteer within the remembered case
roles.noah: Guide assembler within the remembered case

boundaries: Do not invent new case events, timings, quotations, achievements or causal outcomes.
Keep own actions distinct from Maya's and Noah's work.
Clearly label the model as fiction; never insert it into a real learner's personal response.
A private learner may rehearse an ordinary truthful experience, choose another topic or use this labelled fictional case for language practice.
No recording, AI scoring, truth verification, upload or success inferred from a click.
No rigid answer length or required STAR script; these are optional planning distinctions, not official assessment criteria.

blocks.title: Choose What You Can Truthfully Describe
Mark the Boundary of Your Knowledge
Review the Account You Chose to Make

L06.S06.c001.speaker: coach
L06.S06.c001.text: Now prepare a short account of an experience. An ordinary contribution can be worth explaining; you do not need a dramatic achievement. Choose something you can describe truthfully, or use the labelled fictional guide case purely for language practice. Do not present that case as your own biography.
L06.S06.c001.visualEn: Offer two separate routes: Your own truthful experience and Labelled fictional practice. Both remain private. No system-selected personal story or achievement ranking.
L06.S06.c001.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L06.S06.c001.delivery: Calm, concrete teaching; emphasis follows the semantic distinction, with natural pauses.

L06.S06.c002.speaker: coach
L06.S06.c002.text: For a real experience, you may omit names or other private identifiers. Keep the substance accurate. If the topic feels too personal, choose another. The example facts remain available for anyone using the fictional case; they are a reference, not an answer copied into your space.
L06.S06.c002.visualEn: Keep the complete F01–F09 reference readable in a separate case panel when needed. Label it Fictional worked example. The learner’s private-account region stays blank and contains no input or stored response.
L06.S06.c002.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L06.S06.c002.delivery: Calm, concrete teaching; emphasis follows the semantic distinction, with natural pauses.

L06.S06.c003.speaker: coach
L06.S06.c003.text: Ask yourself which part the listener needs: the situation, your contribution, a decision, an observed result, or a reflection. You can use these distinctions to plan, but they are not a required sequence.
L06.S06.c003.visualEn: Reveal optional planning resources without numbered compulsory stages, STAR requirements, official criteria or fixed interview-duration guidance.
L06.S06.c003.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L06.S06.c003.delivery: Calm, concrete teaching; emphasis follows the semantic distinction, with natural pauses.

L06.S06.c004.speaker: coach
L06.S06.c004.text: Keep your own work separate from other people’s contributions. In the guide case, drawing and changing the map belong to the participant; listing the times and assembling the guide do not. Sharing credit makes the account more precise without erasing the participant’s work.
L06.S06.c004.visualEn: Show the established role map, clearly separated from the personal-response area. Use F02/F06 only; no leadership appointment or wider responsibility is added.
L06.S06.c004.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L06.S06.c004.delivery: Calm, concrete teaching; emphasis follows the semantic distinction, with natural pauses.

L06.S06.c005.speaker: coach
L06.S06.c005.text: Privately identify one detail you know and one boundary you should retain. It might be an unmeasured outcome or a future change you have not made. If you use the fictional case, keep its one observed visitor separate from any claim about everyone else.
L06.S06.c005.visualEn: Keep known and unknown regions unfilled for the learner. The fictional one-visitor card remains explicitly a reference, not their personal evidence.
L06.S06.c005.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L06.S06.c005.delivery: Calm, concrete teaching; emphasis follows the semantic distinction, with natural pauses.

L06.S06.c006.speaker: coach
L06.S06.c006.text: Rehearse your account in English. Say it aloud, write privately, or think it through. You may pause or change topics. This player does not record you. If you use the fictional example, keep it labelled as practice rather than presenting it as your own experience.
L06.S06.c006.visualEn: Show the private-rehearsal instructions as readable DOM. No microphone, answer field, generated transcript, achievement score or saved personal record. Keep fiction and personal routes visibly separate.
L06.S06.c006.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L06.S06.c006.delivery: Calm, concrete teaching; emphasis follows the semantic distinction, with natural pauses.

L06.S06.c007.speaker: coach
L06.S06.c007.text: Take some time to put the account together. In Watch, a model follows the thinking pause. In Practice, choose the model when you want to compare approaches, or skip it and continue. You can return for another attempt.
L06.S06.c007.visualEn: Blank private rehearsal board. Show the ordinary Watch/Practice controls and optional model action, with no auto-filled answer or success flag. Keep private area distinct from the fictional case source.
L06.S06.c007.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L06.S06.c007.delivery: Calm, concrete teaching; emphasis follows the semantic distinction, with natural pauses.

L06.S06.c008.speaker: coach
L06.S06.c008.text: For any account you choose to review, check whether your contribution is clear and the result words match what you know. If you have not prepared an account, use the supplied example to examine those two points, then return to your own experience when you are ready.
L06.S06.c008.visualEn: This is the immediate common cue after I03 for every route. Do not refer to hearing the learner, assume model viewing or copy the model into the private area.
L06.S06.c008.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L06.S06.c008.delivery: Calm, concrete teaching; emphasis follows the semantic distinction, with natural pauses.

L06.S06.c009.speaker: coach
L06.S06.c009.text: For a follow-up about what you would change, distinguish a future intention from something already done. For a question about evidence, stay with the observation you can support. You can acknowledge a missing detail instead of constructing a confident answer around it.
L06.S06.c009.visualEn: Introduce both follow-up categories afresh so the shared continuation requires no knowledge of the optional Maya line. Keep future and evidence categories separate.
L06.S06.c009.anchorHint: instead of constructing a confident answer
L06.S06.c009.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L06.S06.c009.delivery: Calm, concrete teaching; emphasis follows the semantic distinction, with natural pauses.

L06.S06.c010.speaker: coach
L06.S06.c010.text: Choose one part to revise privately: clarify your role, narrow a result claim, or mark a future plan as future. You decide what needs attention. No revision is required merely because the model used different words or a different experience.
L06.S06.c010.visualEn: Offer optional revision resources and a blank private area. No mandatory matching, scoring, new gate or automatic replacement sentence.
L06.S06.c010.anchorHint: different words or a different experience
L06.S06.c010.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L06.S06.c010.delivery: Calm, concrete teaching; emphasis follows the semantic distinction, with natural pauses.

L06.S06.c011.speaker: coach
L06.S06.c011.text: Choose relevant details and keep their limits intact. You can return for another attempt, using your own truthful experience or explicitly labelled fiction for language practice.
L06.S06.c011.visualEn: Close neutrally with normal replay controls. No verified-experience badge, mastery statement or automatic next-page navigation.
L06.S06.c011.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L06.S06.c011.delivery: Calm, concrete teaching; emphasis follows the semantic distinction, with natural pauses.

L06.S06.d101.speaker: learner
L06.S06.d101.text: I drew the map for a visitor guide. Maya listed the session times, and Noah assembled the guide. The day before the event, my map said Studio B but the schedule said Blue Room. I checked with the coordinator: both names meant the same room, with Blue Room on the door. I changed my map and told the others. I later saw one visitor use it to find the room. We did not survey visitors, so I cannot say how much the guide helped overall.
L06.S06.d101.visualEn: Show a separate Fictional model account frame with only established F01–F08 facts. No exact coordinator quotation, invented checking duration, expanded impact or real learner autobiography. Keep the real private area blank.
L06.S06.d101.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L06.S06.d101.delivery: Natural collaborative speech; restrained gesture, no exaggerated conflict or comic voice.

L06.S06.d102.speaker: maya
L06.S06.d102.text: What would you do differently if you were preparing another guide?
L06.S06.d102.visualEn: Maya appears as a later authored follow-up partner, never as a flashback speaker at the guide event. The question is not a reaction generated from the real learner’s unheard account.
L06.S06.d102.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L06.S06.d102.delivery: Natural collaborative speech; restrained gesture, no exaggerated conflict or comic voice.

L06.S06.f101.speaker: coach
L06.S06.f101.text: A possible reply would propose agreeing the room names earlier next time. Connect that idea to the mismatch, and keep it in the future: the case has not tested the new approach. You can study this account without copying its events or wording into your own experience.
L06.S06.f101.visualEn: Return to formal model analysis with F09 in the Future proposal region. Do not answer by depicting implementation or a successful second event. No assessment of the real learner.
L06.S06.f101.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L06.S06.f101.delivery: Calm, concrete teaching; emphasis follows the semantic distinction, with natural pauses.

L06.S06.h101.purpose: Privately identify a supported detail and a knowledge boundary.
L06.S06.h101.visualEn: No automatic answer, voice detection, memory inference or truth check.

L06.S06.h102.purpose: Privately review or revise one part without any system evaluation.
L06.S06.h102.visualEn: Keep the private account blank. Do not infer that a truthful answer, spoken attempt or successful revision occurred.

L06.I03.prompt: Privately explain a contribution you made and what you know about its outcome. Use a truthful experience, or explicitly label the guide case as fictional language practice.
L06.I03.skipNote: Skipped. No response has been saved. Continue to the shared explanation.

boundary: Use formal explanation and short explicitly fictional examples. Model events are not learner biography. No inferred recording, truth verification, official rubric or wider outcome.
